type: 实机风格视觉提案，非运行截图或已验证关卡

concepts.prompt:
Create a polished playable-looking 2D Sokoban GAMEPLAY SCREENSHOT, landscape 16:9, same restrained art direction as Patrick's Parabox and Box or Void. True orthographic top-down square grid, solid flat colored square characters with two small square eyes, broad matte wall rims with tiny inset bevel and a short shadow, ivory floor, dark gray background. Very simple geometric visual vocabulary. This is NOT a conceptual illustration, poster, infographic, cover, isometric diorama or cinematic scene. The screen must look like a running finished indie puzzle game paused during a meaningful interaction. Uniform grid spacing, all game entities snap accurately to cells. High visual clarity, restrained palette, no realistic texture, no bloom, no scenery, no character detail. One puzzle room takes 75 percent of image. Small game title and chapter label in upper left margin, compact right-side keycap list "Z 撤回" "R 重置" "Esc 菜单". A subtle one-line hint along the bottom. Do not scatter explanatory callout boxes. Meaning comes from the actual board. Gameplay proposals, no assertion it is a capture from an existing shipped game.
Game title "叠印", level subtitle "03 / 重合的地方，路出现了". 
CORE GAME RULE: the movable boxes are thin square open frames carrying black wall patterns, like solid abstract stencils on a square grid. They can slide across one another. One dark pattern cell makes a wall; exactly TWO overlapping dark cells cancel into walkable cream floor. THREE overlapping dark cells would become wall again. Frame outlines remain visible even where wall cells cancel. The player is one coral square with two dark eyes and can only walk on the final cream floor. Push a frame by standing beside its small solid handle tab. This is local overlap arithmetic, not whole-screen black-white switching.
Show ONE clearly legible 11x9-grid room with solid charcoal rim and cream base floor. Exactly two large movable stencil frames, each 5 by 5 grid cells: a muted blue frame slightly left and below center, a muted amber frame slightly right and above center, with a 3-cell-wide overlap strip in the middle. Frame rim is very thin and grid-aligned, not a solid thick wall. Each frame carries a sparse pattern of dark navy wall tiles arranged as small corner shapes and barriers, with openings. Essential visual reveal: where the two patterns cross in the central shared strip, a run of matching dark squares CANCELS into THREE cream walkable squares forming a small clear corridor. Distinguish these cancelled floor squares with subtle tiny blue-and-amber opposing corner notches (not hatching), so one sees both frames are responsible. Outside the shared strip, the same bar continues as dark blocked squares. The corridor is unmistakably in the actual board, not a secondary diagram.
Place player just outside the left side of the blue frame, immediately adjacent to its small blue handle at mid-height, ready to push it right. A one-cell-wide thin blue dashed preview edge to the right indicates the next frame position, unobtrusive. Place one small white eye-outline player exit in the upper-right open floor pocket, reachable by the corridor once aligned. Two colored corner-shaped docking marks at the perimeter can indicate frame goals, no conventional crates or extra characters. Use a sparse level, not a sea of squares. Blue and amber outlines remain distinguishable and exactly follow cell borders. Add a small inline HUD legend below the title using three tiny actual grid icons "1层：墙    2层：路    3层：墙", subdued. Bottom hint exact Chinese "重叠会开路，也会改变你的退路". The central cancellation corridor must be the visual focus. Small screenshot typography, no giant text.

Game title "牵引", level subtitle "04 / 隔着墙，把它拉出来".
CORE GAME RULE: two boxes are connected by one fixed-length visible cord. The player pushes a box normally. Slack first disappears; once the cord is taut, pushing one endpoint away pulls the other endpoint along the cord's route. Cord bends around solid wall corners. No teleportation, no moving on its own, no gears or magic beam. Show a single highly readable situation explaining this through spatial layout.
One 11x9 grid room, thick slate-lavender rim, cream floor. In the center a 4-cell-wide by 3-cell-high rectangular wall island divides the left and right lanes, connected by an open upper route. Exactly two solid teal square crates, one in the lower left lane, one in the right lane near its closed lower end. A single warm amber cord connects their centers, running UP from the left crate, then horizontally above the central wall island, then DOWN along its right side to the right crate: a clear inverted-U cord. Cord remains precisely on walkable cells and curves gently around the two top wall corners, NEVER crosses through any wall. At the corners use tiny restrained brass guide-edge details integrated into the wall, not extra machines.
Place the left crate at a position with one free floor cell BELOW it. Its pink square player is immediately ABOVE it, preparing to push it DOWN. Outline the next cell below the left crate with a thin teal dashed destination; it contains a goal. Place the right crate at a dead end with solid wall immediately BELOW it, so the player could not stand behind it and push it up. The cell immediately ABOVE this right crate is clear and contains the second goal; outline it with a thin teal dashed destination. The taut U-shaped cord shows how pushing the LEFT crate DOWN pulls the RIGHT crate UP out of this trap. Exactly two tiny near-box direction preview arrows, down at left and up at right. No large diagram arrows outside the level. Precisely ONE player, TWO crates, TWO goals, ONE continuous unbranched cord. Avoid knot tangles or floating detached rope.
A small unobtrusive cord-length indicator by the selected left crate reads "绳已绷紧". Bottom hint exact Chinese "推这一端，拉动另一端". The spatial irony should be clear: the right crate is against a wall but can be retrieved indirectly. Subtle squeeze on the selected left crate, short clean shadows. Everything as minimal and solid as the earlier Box or Void-inspired screenshots.
